name: Venus Remedies
tagline: Turned-around, debt-free injectables/oncology exporter whose FY26 filings confirm the inflection is cash-backed (CFO >= EBITDA two years running) - still only ~19x earnings, though ~Rs 23 Cr of FY26 margin was one-offs and promoter holding is only ~42%
business_overview: Venus Remedies manufactures complex injectable formulations (critical care and oncology) for regulated and semi-regulated markets, with 1,100+ granted market authorizations. Historically debt-laden and defaulted around 2015 (a similar trajectory to Wockhardt), the company sold its Elores business to Cipla in 2020, used the proceeds to eliminate debt, and has since transformed into a debt-free, cash-generative business with an increasing Oncology mix alongside its legacy Carbapenem (antibiotics) franchise. It also has an early-stage NCE pipeline (VRP-034, VRP-048) with FDA QIDP (fast-track) status.

fundamentals_narrative: FY26 filings substantially de-risk the prior 'needs to prove out' caveat. Consolidated revenue Rs 769.6 Cr (+17.9%), EBITDA Rs 159.9 Cr at a 20.8% margin (vs 12.9% FY25), consolidated PAT Rs 102.8 Cr (+127%). Q4 FY26 was a record (sales Rs 259.4 Cr, 24.45% OPM, +960bps YoY); the latest quarter normalised back to ~Rs 179 Cr revenue / ~20% OPM / ~Rs 26 Cr PAT - still well ahead of the year-ago quarter. Crucially the earnings are cash-backed: FY26 operating cash flow of ~Rs 151-155 Cr matched or exceeded EBITDA for the second year running, and trade receivables actually fell (Rs 112 Cr -> Rs 103 Cr) despite the revenue growth - evidence the reported profit is real. The balance sheet is now effectively debt-free (borrowings ~Rs 12 Cr) with >Rs 250 Cr cash/investments and zero promoter pledge (SEBI-confirmed for FY26); first dividend in 13 years paid (Rs 10 final, approved at the 37th AGM on 20-Aug-2026). Two tempering points: (1) ~Rs 23 Cr of FY26 operating profit was one-offs - an Rs 11 Cr Cipla/Elores milestone and ~Rs 11.8 Cr PLI incentive - so normalised OPM is ~17%, not 20.8%; (2) management previously set (and missed) a Rs 1,000 Cr FY25 revenue target, so the market applies a discount to any new guidance. Capex is internal/organic, focused on lyophilisation where capacity currently meets only about half of demand. R&D held at ~2.4% of sales; VRP-034 (AMR, FDA QIDP) and in-licensed MET-X remain zero-ascribed optionality. Exports >Rs 590 Cr in FY26 (LatAm 24.2%, Europe 22.6%).

phreakv6 (trusted, core-tier) took a disclosed position on a peer-valuation-gap thesis; the gap is still open - Venus trades at ~19x P/E / ~9x EV/EBITDA vs materially richer listed peers on similar oncology/anti-infective profitability

verdict_headline: FY26 filings confirm a cash-backed turnaround and the peer-valuation gap is still open at ~19x - conviction holds at High, with the one-off adjustment and guidance-credibility discount as the standing caveats
verdict_reasoning: The prior note's central uncertainty - 'FY27 needs to prove out, one-off risk' - is substantially de-risked: a record Q4, full-year revenue +18%, and two consecutive years of operating cash flow matching or exceeding EBITDA (with receivables falling) show the profit inflection is durable and real, not accounting-led

The valuation-gap thesis phreakv6 (trusted, core-tier) and vikas_sinha bought is still intact - ~19x P/E / ~9x EV/EBITDA / ~3x book, and the 2.5x price move to date came from earnings doubling rather than any re-rating

Caveats remain and are now quantified: ~Rs 23 Cr of FY26 margin was one-offs (normalised OPM ~17%), management has a missed-target credibility discount, promoter holding is only ~42%, and there are still no concalls

Net: conviction High -> High (confirmed). Thesis-fit stays 10x-in-2-3-years - the organic lyophilisation capacity lever plus un-priced NCE optionality, on a debt-free balance sheet at an undemanding multiple, keeps the asymmetric case alive
